builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Calibrate Once, Grow the Vocabulary: Candidate-Independent Scores for Conformal Risk Control in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
summary: The method replaces per-vocabulary conformal recalibration with scoring each candidate label against a fixed reference bank, making scores invariant to added class names so one calibration retains its risk guarantee as the vocabulary grows. It costs no training and little overhead, but prediction sets can grow by up to roughly one extra label per pixel, and the bounded miss rate for added names holds only if annotated names are a random sample of names in the calibration images, with excess bounded by the gap in mean miss rate otherwise. It can fail when that random-sample assumption is violated, e.g., when harder or adversarially chosen names are added, and it applies only to open-vocabulary segmentation or detection pipelines that use conformal risk control.
rationale: The technique is training-free and cheap to implement, but it only matters for teams running open-vocabulary segmentation with conformal risk control, so it warrants a small-scale validation on the reader's actual segmenter rather than blanket adoption.
technique: Candidate-independent conformal scoring via fixed reference bank

claims.statement: The method replaces per-vocabulary conformal recalibration with scoring each candidate label against a fixed reference bank, making scores invariant to added class names so one calibration retains its risk guarantee as the vocabulary grows. It costs no training and little overhead, but prediction sets can grow by up to roughly one extra label per pixel, and the bounded miss rate for added names holds only if annotated names are a random sample of names in the calibration images, with excess bounded by the gap in mean miss rate otherwise. It can fail when that random-sample assumption is violated, e.g., when harder or adversarially chosen names are added, and it applies only to open-vocabulary segmentation or detection pipelines that use conformal risk control.

Applied to Grounding DINO, which splits large vocabularies into chunks, the conversion makes inference about six times faster; for CAT-Seg and SED at alpha=10%, converted models use at most one more label per pixel than released models recalibrated at the grown vocabulary.
